🇬🇲🇪🇺: The European Union Election Observation Mission on Thursday deployed 16 long-term observers across The Gambia’s seven regions ahead of the 5 December 2026 presidential election, with 20 short-term observers set to join them closer to polling day. This is the third EU observation mission to the country since 2017. Chief Observer Reinhold Lopatka said the mission would remain impartial, assess the process against Gambian law and international standards, and issue its first conclusions two days after election day. 

He described the vote as an opportunity for The Gambia to strengthen its democratic institutions and thanked the authorities for the invitation. Deputy Chief Observer Stéphane Mondon added that the mission would also monitor media, social media and the use of state resources, releasing quantitative and qualitative findings at the same post-election press conference. The observers will cover the full electoral cycle, from the legal framework and campaign financing to voting, counting, complaints and the participation of women, young people and persons with disabilities.

(VOD Media)
